title: Steganographic PowerShell loader opened full-access LSASS handles on SCRANTON and NASHUA
rationale: Same events: hidden steganography-launched PowerShell (PID 2976) on scranton opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff at 03:05:16Z, and wsmprovhost.exe on nashua opened lsass with 0x1f3fff at 03:09:29Z. Full-access LSASS handle opens are best described as LSASS memory credential dumping; no auth-process modification or API hooking was directly evidenced.

title: SAM_SERVER handles requested on SCRANTON
rationale: lsass on scranton requested SAM_SERVER handles with 0xf003f at 03:19-03:20; no dump file observed — SAM credential access attempt.

title: Get-Keystrokes keylogger and clipboard collection on SCRANTON
rationale: Same pbeesly session: Get-Clipboard, Keystroke-Check AV check, then Get-Keystrokes background job viewed and removed — keylogging.

title: WebDAV forced authentication from SCRANTON to attacker server 192.168.0.4
rationale: DavClnt/WebDAV-MiniRedir sequence drove 10.0.1.4 to authenticate (AUTHORIZATION header, pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL) to 192.168.0.4 and download payloads — forced authentication.

title: Password-targeted file collection and encrypted archiving on SCRANTON and NASHUA
rationale: Same collection action: recursive enumeration of user profile for credential-named files (*psw*, *pass*, *login*, *admin*, *vpn*) compressed into working.zip on nashua and OfficeSupplies.7z on scranton, then Rar-encrypted and sdelete-wiped — credentials in files.

title: Registry value read and piped to Invoke-Expression on SCRANTON
rationale: Get-ItemPropertyValue 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Javasoft' 'value Supplement' | Invoke-Expression — registry-stored payload/credential pattern; no registry credential read confirmed.

title: Get-PrivateKeys exported LocalMachine certificates to password-protected .pfx on SCRANTON
rationale: Same script block (Get-PrivateKeys from readme.ps1) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and calling Export-PfxCertificate to Downloads\coyn5igj.3io.pfx with hardcoded password 'saribas' — private key theft.

title: SMB/WinRM authentication traffic duplicated across two L2 paths
rationale: Kerberos/GSSAPI SMB and WinRM sessions from 10.0.1.4 to 10.0.1.6 recorded twice with different MAC pairs — shape of SMB relay/name-resolution interception; WPAD queries answered normally.

title: Same IP 10.0.1.4 on two L2 addresses toward 10.0.1.6
rationale: Duplicate flows with source IP 10.0.1.4 but two different MAC pairs — possible ARP cache poisoning/on-path host.

title: Credential material accessed on SCRANTON but no offline cracking observed
rationale: LSASS handle opens and certificate export occurred, but no hashcat/Mimikatz/SAM/NTDS cracking evidence — the observed action is credential dumping, not password cracking.

title: PsExec64 with plaintext credentials delivered python.exe implant to NASHUA
rationale: Same events: Invoke-SeaDukeStage and PsExec64 -u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by launching C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on NASHUA, which beacons over TLS to 192.168.0.4:8443 — remote execution/lateral movement, not credential access.

title: csc.exe compiled in-memory loader DLLs from hidden PowerShell on SCRANTON
rationale: csc.exe compiling loader DLLs in Temp under hidden PowerShell — compile-after-delivery execution, not credential access.

title: Credential material exfiltrated to attacker WebDAV share 192.168.0.4
rationale: Invoke-Exfil compressed Downloads into OfficeSupplies.7z and copied it to \\192.168.0.4\webdav — exfiltration to attacker-controlled share, not credential access.

title: Credential-access chain staged via sdclt/control.exe and PsExec-delivered python.exe
rationale: Summary finding of the sdclt.exe→control.exe→hidden PowerShell stager and PsExec-delivered python.exe chain; the underlying actions are covered by the LSASS, forced-auth, and lateral-movement incidents, and the chain itself is PowerShell execution.

title: No on-host AiTM tooling; Temp python.exe via PsExec unrelated to AiTM
rationale: Only network-adjacent executions are Azure guest-agent diagnostics; the unusual process is PsExec-launched C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe — remote execution, not adversary-in-the-middle.

title: accesschk.exe permission discovery on SCRANTON
rationale: accesschk.exe run from attacker-staged SysinternalsSuite for permission discovery — discovery, not credential access.

title: Credential-access tooling and anti-forensics in the SCRANTON PowerShell session
rationale: Summary finding combining sdelete64 secure deletion, accesschk execution, Get-PrivateKeys export, and Get-Keystrokes; the credential actions are covered by the certificate, keylogging, and LSASS incidents, and the distinct action here is indicator removal.

title: Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe used to encrypt and wipe collected data on NASHUA
rationale: Rar.exe password-encrypted working.zip and sdelete64 wiped the tool and archive — defense evasion/indicator removal, not credential access.

title: Explicit-credential logons are pbeesly reusing its own credentials to NASHUA via PsExec
rationale: All 4648 events involve pbeesly's own credentials to NASHUA via PSEXESVC; no spraying pattern — valid account use, not brute force.

title: sdclt.exe abused to spawn hidden PowerShell on SCRANTON
rationale: sdclt.exe launched from cmd spawning hidden PowerShell — signed binary proxy execution, not credential access.

title: hostui.exe launched with runas by PowerShell on SCRANTON
rationale: PowerShell started hostui.exe -verb runas to elevate before the HKLM Javasoft payload — privilege escalation via UAC bypass, not credential access.
